name: Work Permit (migrant worker)

requirements.blocker_text: This is restricted to specific designated sectors: construction, manufacturing, marine/shipyard, process, services, and foreign domestic work.
This is restricted to nationals of an approved source country/region, which varies by sector.
This requires the employer to have available quota under the sector-specific Dependency Ratio Ceiling and to pay the applicable foreign-worker levy.

evidence_required.document: Employment contract with an employer in an approved sector

outcome.duration_length: up to 2 years, renewable subject to age limits and sector-specific caps on total years

sources.title: Work Permit for foreign worker - Ministry of Manpower

notes: GENUINE STRUCTURAL FLOOR of Singapore's work-pass hierarchy — deliberately terminal (leads_to_pr: false, no citizenship path, family_can_join: false), a real and confirmed policy design rather than an oversight, distinguishing it sharply from S Pass and Employment Pass above it. Restricted to nationals of approved source countries per sector — a genuine eligibility gate absent from every higher-tier Singapore pass in this dataset, meaning nationality itself is a hard predicate here in a way it isn't for EP/S Pass/ONE Pass. Foreign Domestic Worker permits are administered as a sub-category of this same Work Permit framework with their own distinct rules (levy concessions, mandatory rest days, employer eligibility criteria) — not modeled as a separate requirement group here given the scope of this research pass; flagged as a real simplification. This is the closest Singapore analogue to the lower-tier, non-settlement-track routes seen in other countries' datasets (e.g. UK/Netherlands seasonal-adjacent categories), though Singapore's version is structurally starker in explicitly foreclosing any path to settlement.
